title: Aft Fuselage — Aft Cargo Compartment Wiring and Sill Route

issue.reason: Original issue of the aft cargo compartment wiring and sill route sheet.

ata.title: Aft Fuselage Wiring — Aft Cargo Wiring

abstract: Wiring diagram for the aft cargo compartment, showing the sill route that carries the compartment lighting, the smoke detection sampling harness and the aft fuselage terminal block feeds.

sections.purpose: This sheet shows the wiring of the aft cargo compartment, including the compartment lighting feed, the smoke detection harness and the terminal block distribution at the aft fuselage.
sections.sheet_note: The compartment lighting and the smoke detection harnesses share the sill route along the lower edge of the compartment, which is the only continuous path between stations C52 and C66 that stays clear of the loading rail. The two harnesses are separated by a bonded conduit rather than by distance, so any structural work that disturbs the sill route affects both systems at once. Terminal block positions are shown at their frame stations rather than by dimension.
sections.routing_note: The sill route runs along the lower edge of the compartment from station C52 to station C66 at a nominal 40 mm from the frame lower flange, supported on stand-off clips at 250 mm pitch. It crosses to the belly fairing at station C64 to reach the aft fuselage terminal block. The clearance between the route and the frame lower flange is the tightest point of the installation and is called out on sheet 2.

ata.title: Aft Fuselage Wiring — Aft Cargo Wiring

abstract: Wiring diagram for the aft cargo compartment, showing the sill route that carries the compartment lighting, the smoke detection sampling harness and the aft fuselage terminal block feeds, with the joint drain outlets shown as keep-clear positions.

sections.purpose: This sheet shows the wiring of the aft cargo compartment, including the compartment lighting feed, the smoke detection harness and the terminal block distribution at the aft fuselage.
sections.sheet_note: The compartment lighting and the smoke detection harnesses share the sill route along the lower edge of the compartment, which is the only continuous path between stations C52 and C66 that stays clear of the loading rail. The two harnesses are separated by a bonded conduit rather than by distance, so any structural work that disturbs the sill route affects both systems at once. Terminal block positions are shown at their frame stations rather than by dimension. The drain outlets shown on sheet 2 are a structural feature carried on this sheet for clearance only; nothing electrical is connected to them.
sections.routing_note: The sill route runs along the lower edge of the compartment from station C52 to station C66 at a nominal 40 mm from the frame lower flange, supported on stand-off clips at 250 mm pitch. It crosses to the belly fairing at station C64 to reach the aft fuselage terminal block. The clearance between the route and the frame lower flange is the tightest point of the installation and is called out on sheet 2. The four drain outlets of the longitudinal joint sealing standard are shown on sheet 2 at their agreed position, 40 mm inboard of the outlets first proposed, so that water leaving the joint falls clear of the stand-off clip line; no clip may be moved into the shaded band beneath an outlet, and a clip disturbed for structural work is put back on its original stand-off and not on the nearest convenient one.
